basics.description: **Note:** Please refer to the following before installing the solution: • Review the solution [Release Notes](https://github.com/Azure/Azure-Sentinel/tree/master/Solutions/Databricks/ReleaseNotes.md) • There may be [known issues](https://aka.ms/sentinelsolutionsknownissues) pertaining to this Solution, please refer to them before installing. The [Databricks](https://www.databricks.com/) solution for Microsoft Sentinel ingests the account and workspace [audit logs](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/admin/account-settings/audit-logs) that Databricks on AWS delivers to Amazon S3, using the Codeless Connector Framework S3 poller. No Function App or AWS access keys are needed. **Underlying Microsoft Technologies used:** a. [Codeless Connector Framework](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/sentinel/create-codeless-connector) **Pre-requisites:** 1. Databricks Premium or Enterprise tier with audit log delivery to S3 (JSON). 2. Rights to deploy the solution's two CloudFormation templates and add an S3 event notification. **Data Connectors:** 1, **Analytic Rules:** 4, **Hunting Queries:** 3 [Learn more about Microsoft Sentinel](https://aka.ms/azuresentinel) | [Learn more about Solutions](https://aka.ms/azuresentinelsolutionsdoc)

options.text: This Solution installs the data connector for Databricks Audit Logs via Amazon S3 (via Codeless Connector Framework). You can get Databricks Audit Logs via Amazon S3 (via Codeless Connector Framework) data in your Microsoft Sentinel workspace. After installing the solution, configure and enable this data connector by following guidance in Manage solution view.

link.label: Learn more about connecting data sources

options.text: This solution installs the following analytic rule templates. After installing the solution, create and enable analytic rules in Manage solution view.

elements.name: analytic1
elements.label: Databricks - Multiple failed logins from a single IP

options.text: Identifies ten or more failed Databricks login attempts from one source IP address within an hour, which can indicate password guessing or credential stuffing against a workspace or the account console.

elements.name: analytic2
elements.label: Databricks - Account or workspace admin privilege granted

options.text: Identifies a user or service principal being made a Databricks account or workspace admin, or added to the admins group. Admin access controls clusters, data access and secrets, so grants should be rare and expected.

elements.name: analytic3
elements.label: Databricks - IP access list or network setting changed

options.text: Identifies creation, modification or deletion of a Databricks IP access list, or a change to the setting that enables IP access lists. Loosening these controls opens the workspace to previously blocked addresses.

elements.name: analytic4
elements.label: Databricks - Personal access token created with long or no expiry

options.text: Identifies a Databricks personal access token created with a lifetime over 90 days or no expiry. Long-lived tokens outlive interactive session controls and are a common persistence method after account compromise.
This solution installs the following hunting queries. After installing the solution, run these hunting queries to hunt for threats in Manage solution view.

elements.name: huntingquery1
elements.label: Databricks - Secret reads outside business hours

options.text: Lists Databricks secret reads (getSecret) from 19:00 to 07:00 UTC in the last 7 days, by user and source IP. Off-hours reads can indicate credential harvesting. Adjust the hours to your time zone. This hunting query depends on DatabricksAuditLogs data connector (DatabricksAudit_CL Parser or Table)

elements.name: huntingquery2
elements.label: Databricks - Notebook exports and large result downloads

options.text: Lists notebook exports and downloads of query or notebook results in the last 7 days, by user. A spike in exports or downloads by one user, or exports from a user who does not normally perform them, can indicate data exfiltration. This hunting query depends on DatabricksAuditLogs data connector (DatabricksAudit_CL Parser or Table)

elements.name: huntingquery3
elements.label: Databricks - User activity from a source IP not seen in the previous 14 days

options.text: Lists users whose Databricks activity in the last day came from a source IP not seen for that user in the previous 14 days. Review together with token creation, secret reads or admin actions. This hunting query depends on DatabricksAuditLogs data connector (DatabricksAudit_CL Parser or Table)
